transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over a Unix socket, newline-delimited
identity: derived from the connection (SO_PEERCRED on the socket, the bearer on HTTP — ADR-0082); never a parameter (I2). `null` values are refused: omit the field.
roles: reader < agent < reviewer < admin (AUTH-4); each verb's `role` is the least it needs, and a call above the caller's role is refused -32602 naming both.

errors.-32602: invalid params / refused with the reason; a field the verb does not list here is refused by name (I7); a verb above the caller's role names the role needed (AUTH-4)
errors.-32014: the semantic reviewer refused: a workflow blocker (ADR-0048 d4), never an approval and never a demand for a human — the row stays where it was

verbs.name: dg.approval
verbs.summary: Who approved one artifact, or why it waits — a read model folded from its journal, never a state. `status` is one of rejected | refused | vetoed | withdrawn | countersigned | human_approved | ai_approved | escalated | pending | not_applicable; `signers[]` lists every decision with the signer's class (human | model | org | deployment | agent), the model label off the verdict, and whether it counts toward k.
verbs.returns: object: {artifact_id, state, status, reason, k_required, k_have, signers[], approved_by{model,human,org}, model_labels[], provisional, human_veto_available, human_sign_available, decisions[], veto?, open_objections, revision}

verbs.name: dg.audit
verbs.summary: The decisions about one artifact with signatures verified.

verbs.name: dg.away
verbs.summary: The operator declares an absence (ADR-0045): the human-review TTLs stop until `back`, the time away subtracted on restart. Nothing is promoted meanwhile.

params.name: until
params.description: ms epoch; the hold's own ceiling — past it the TTLs run again

verbs.returns: object: {away, declared, since, days, until?, note?}

verbs.name: dg.back
verbs.summary: The operator is back: the clocks restart with the time away subtracted (ADR-0045).

verbs.name: dg.ban
verbs.summary: Refuse a writer's, or a source prefix's, next ingest at the door with -32009 (ADR-0052 d6). Operator only; touches nothing already admitted (I4); not replicated.

params.name: subject
params.description: the identity, or a source_uri prefix

params.name: reason
params.description: required unless lift — it is what the refused writer is told

params.name: lift
params.description: true lifts a ban in effect

verbs.name: dg.bans
verbs.summary: The bans in effect and what they refused at the door (ADR-0052 d6). Read-only; `status` carries the same list.

verbs.name: dg.comment
verbs.summary: Record a remark on an artifact — an annotation, never a decision. Changes nothing about the row's standing and counts toward nothing; an open `objection` by the operator holds auto-promotion until a `resolution` replies to it or it is retracted. The author class (human/model/agent) is derived from the signing identity, never a parameter (I2). Comments are never published (I1) and never leave this gate.

params.name: artifact_id
params.description: the row to comment on; any state

params.name: kind
params.description: note | question | objection | resolution; default note

params.name: reply_to
params.description: a live comment on the same artifact; required for a resolution

params.name: findings
params.description: finding kinds on the row this remark is about

errors.-32602: unknown artifact, bad kind, empty body, reply_to not a live comment here

verbs.name: dg.comment_retract
verbs.summary: Withdraw a comment: its author, or the operator. The comment stays as a tombstone; an open objection retracted this way releases the hold it held.

errors.-32602: unknown comment, already retracted, or not yours to retract

verbs.name: dg.comments
verbs.summary: The comment thread on one artifact, oldest first, with counts (total, open human objections).

params.name: include_retracted
params.description: default false — tombstones are kept in the projection

verbs.name: dg.crawler_policy
verbs.summary: Issue or retrieve a source-scoped, expiring robots exception on the deployment journal. Never exposed as an MCP tool.

params.name: scope_hash
params.description: sha256 of canonical crawler source scope

verbs.name: dg.defer
verbs.summary: Record that the operator looked and moved on (F40). Not a lifecycle transition.

verbs.name: dg.demote
verbs.summary: Withdraw an admitted artifact from every consumer surface; the content is kept.

verbs.name: dg.describe
verbs.summary: This catalog, for the answering daemon's role — the socket describing itself — plus `you`: who the gate took the caller for and the role every verb is held to (ADR-0082).
verbs.returns: object: {service, version, role, verbs[], documents{}, you{identity, role, kind}}

verbs.name: dg.engagement
verbs.summary: Did the operator actually review? Counts over a window.

verbs.name: dg.grade
verbs.summary: Run the gate engine on one artifact: one model call per stance, one verdict per item.

verbs.name: dg.grade_pending
verbs.summary: Grade what waits at L1, within the day's budget (fail-closed when spent, I6).

verbs.name: dg.graph
verbs.summary: The constellation: every artifact as a node, every relation edge, every pin, every ban — the ADR-0035 projection serialized at once, bounded. `label` and `source_uri` are carried only for ACTIVE / SUPERSEDED rows (INV-SEC-10): a held artifact is its existence, never its content. `revision` is the journal tip; pass it back as `if_revision` and an unchanged graph answers {revision, unchanged: true}.

params.name: limit
params.description: nodes, newest state change first; default and ceiling 2000

params.name: if_revision
params.description: the revision the caller already holds

verbs.returns: object: {revision, unchanged} | {revision, full, nodes[], edges[], pins[], bans[], total, truncated, counts, spaces, states, viewer}

verbs.name: dg.hide
verbs.summary: Stop serving a promoted artifact to one audience, or to all — reversibly (ADR-0052 d4). The row stays ACTIVE and why-able; include_hidden returns it. A total hide by a non-operator is journaled `lowered`.

params.name: lift
params.description: true reverses an earlier hide for this audience — a second event, both kept

verbs.returns: object: {artifact_id, audience, hidden, event_id, hidden_for[], lowered?}

verbs.name: dg.ingest
verbs.summary: Propose content. Scanned before this answers (ADR-0053 d1) and lands in quarantine at L1 (or L1b on a finding); nothing is readable until promoted. Writer identity is the connection's, never a parameter (I2).

params.name: content
params.description: utf-8 text, or base64 with encoding='base64'

params.name: content_type
params.description: bundle_asset | bundle_document | bundle_python | bundle_skill | derived_fact | imported_document | memory | prompt_template | skill | skill_archive | summary | bundle_manifest | event | fetch | generation | message | message_part | scratchpad_state | session | state_snapshot | tool_call | trace | usage_record | verdict; the second group is the recorded path (taxonomy §2.2) — written and replayable, never graded as a belief; an unregistered type enters at the strictest class (FR-18)

params.name: source_uri
params.description: where it came from, e.g. agent://hermes/session-42

params.name: space
params.description: the folder within the deployment; default main (ADR-0023)

params.name: derives_from
params.description: parent artifact ids (provenance edges, frozen in the envelope)

verbs.returns: object: {artifact_id, state, findings_count, scan_event} — the scanner's rule pass ran before this answered (ADR-0053 d1); state is L1_SCANNED or L1B_FLAGGED, and a finding's text is never in the answer

verbs.name: dg.ingest_bundle
verbs.summary: Inspect a ZIP without execution. Retain the original archive, its complete canonical manifest and every scanned file occurrence in quarantine, all at T-5 (the daemon proposes the class; the verb takes none). Fetch evidence must match the retained body's hash, size, successful status and URL — consistency, not network attestation. Writer is the connection identity. Validation never authorizes installation or promotion.

params.name: source_uri
params.description: must match the fetch's final_url (or url if absent), ignoring the URI fragment — a connector's `#fetch=…` label never reaches the wire

params.name: fetch_artifact_id
params.description: same-space retained fetch artifact: content_hash, bytes, status, url/final_url

params.name: manifest
params.description: optional SDK v1 manifest, recomputed completely against the archive bytes

verbs.returns: object: {state: quarantined, validation: valid|failed, archive_artifact_id, manifest_artifact_id, members: [{path, content_hash, size_bytes, classification, artifact_id, state, scan_event}], reason?}. Failed validation retains the archive only, and `reason` is one of: fetch_missing | fetch_wrong_type | fetch_wrong_space | fetch_blob_mismatch | fetch_mismatch:<field> | archive_invalid:<detail>. An invalid fetch never creates a provenance edge. No model judgment or installation.

errors.-32006: quarantine full; interrupted writes remain held

verbs.name: dg.inventory
verbs.summary: Every artifact in EVERY lifecycle state, as metadata, paged and filterable — the operator workspace's list. Deliberately wider than dg.pending, which answers about quarantine only and so can never show the ACTIVE row a handoff is made from. Carries the spaces the store actually holds, because a caller that cannot name a space cannot pass `spaces` to dg.recall, and a recall without it falls back to `main` and answers nothing. Metadata only: no content, ever.

params.name: states
params.description: restrict to these lifecycle states; default all. Unknown names are ignored

params.name: spaces
params.description: restrict to these spaces; default all

params.name: q
params.description: substring match on artifact id, content type or writer identity

verbs.returns: object: {artifacts[], total, offset, limit, counts{state: n}, spaces[], states[]} — `counts` is over the filtered set, `spaces` and `states` are the whole store's vocabulary so a filter control can be rendered from the answer itself

verbs.name: dg.keys
verbs.summary: API keys (AUTH-3): list the key table, issue a `dgk_…` key (shown once; stored as its hash in an `apikey-issued` event) with a role no higher than the caller's, or revoke one by id.

params.name: label
params.description: who or what holds the key (issue)

params.name: role
params.description: reader | agent | reviewer | admin; default agent (issue)

verbs.returns: object: list → {keys[{key_id, label, role, issued_by, issued_at, expires_at, revoked_at}]}; issue → {key, key_id, role, label, expires_at, event_id}; revoke → {key_id, revoked, already?, event_id?} + the list

errors.-32602: unknown action, bad role, unknown key_id, or a role above the issuer's

verbs.name: dg.node
verbs.summary: One node in full for a review surface: the status row, the approval trail, the comment thread, relations, the served tip, bundle members (`derives_from` children), and a bounded MASKED preview (INV-SEC-7; null when the content is erased or the blob is gone). The org gate's `read` scope sees promoted rows only.
verbs.returns: object: {artifact_id, status, approval, comments, relations, tip, members[], preview, preview_chars, self_authored, refusal?, revision}

verbs.name: dg.override_tip
verbs.summary: Pin a chain's served head to this member (time travel). Reversible by a second override.

verbs.name: dg.pending
verbs.summary: What is waiting in quarantine, as metadata (state, class, kind) — never content.

verbs.name: dg.people
verbs.summary: The role table (ADR-0082 d5, AUTH-4): list every identity this gate has a role for, assign a role to an (iss, sub), or remove one. A role never exceeds the assigner's. `list` also shows the built-in issuer's people and `[auth].admins`.

params.name: iss
params.description: the issuer; default this gate's person issuer

params.name: sub
params.description: the subject at that issuer (assign, remove)

verbs.returns: object: list → {issuer, people[{iss, sub, role, source, email?, name?, assigned_by?, assigned_at?}]}; assign → {iss, sub, role, event_id} + the list; remove → {iss, sub, removed, was?, event_id?} + the list

errors.-32602: unknown action, bad role, missing sub, or a role above the assigner's

verbs.name: dg.ping
verbs.summary: Liveness and identity: deployment id, role, retrieval paths, degraded flags, quorum profile.
verbs.returns: object: {pong, deployment_id, role, paths, degraded, quorum_profile}

verbs.name: dg.promote
verbs.summary: Admit an artifact whose quorum is met. On a solo client the promotion is provisional until an org gate countersigns (R3).

params.name: supersedes
params.description: parent id this artifact supersedes (single-head chains, ADR-0035)

verbs.name: dg.publish
verbs.summary: The note publisher's cursors: status | poll | rewind <sink> [--to <event>] (ADR-0031).

verbs.name: dg.rank
verbs.summary: A weight for one audience (ADR-0052). recall(audience=…) multiplies the hit by it; 1.0 when none — less likely, never absent. Any non-writer identity, human or agent; the writer is refused (I2).

params.name: audience
params.description: a string the caller chooses; nothing validates it against a taxonomy

params.name: weight
params.description: in (0, 10.0]; 1.0 is neutral and zero is what `hide` is for. A console reads this as 1-100 logarithmically, 50 neutral (ADR-0058 §2)

verbs.name: dg.rebuild
verbs.summary: Replay the journal into every projection; the result must equal the live state (I5).

verbs.name: dg.recall
verbs.summary: Read the active store, plus the caller's own scanned claims still in quarantine marked unreviewed (ADR-0053 d2). Nobody else's quarantine, ever (I1). Provisional hits are marked; superseded are hidden unless asked for.

params.name: spaces
params.description: restrict to these spaces; default all the caller may read

params.name: audience
params.description: ADR-0052 d2: the reader's preference, an argument never an identity — each hit's fused score is multiplied by its rank for this audience (1.0 when none) and hides for it apply; omitted = today's answer, byte for byte

params.name: include_hidden
params.description: ADR-0052 d4: rows hidden for this audience (or for all) are dropped before fusion; true returns them, each marked provenance.hidden

params.name: include_own_pending
params.description: ADR-0053 d2 (FR-13): default true — the caller's OWN scanned, unflagged claims still in quarantine are appended after the ranked hits, each `ratified: false`, `provenance.unreviewed: true`, with its state; never anyone else's, never L0 or L1b

verbs.name: dg.reconcile
verbs.summary: Re-derive the consumer surfaces from the journal (the integrator's rebuild).

verbs.name: dg.reject
verbs.summary: Refuse an artifact in quarantine, with a category and optionally what it lost to (ADR-0037).

verbs.name: dg.relate
verbs.summary: Append a typed relation from artifact_id (child) to parent: supersedes | restates | corrects | contradicts | extends. Only supersedes hides.

verbs.name: dg.relations
verbs.summary: The typed relation edges touching one artifact (ADR-0035).

verbs.name: dg.review
verbs.summary: The operator's queue: what needs a human, capped. Each row is annotated with a bounded content preview, whether the operator wrote it (I2), and the verdicts its state accepts.

verbs.name: dg.review_pending
verbs.summary: ADR-0048: the second opinion. Under review.mode model|auto, every L2 row whose first pass escalated gets one `gate-review` verdict, charged to the same budget; a no-op under `human`. Never touches L1b (INV-SEC-5).

verbs.name: dg.review_runs
verbs.summary: The review-run log: bounded, filterable, searchable, newest first. Deliberately separate from dg.status's queue depths — a depth is what is WAITING, a run is what is being PROCESSED, and reading one as the other is the misreport this split prevents.

params.name: state
params.description: queued | running | completed | failed | blocked | all; default all

params.name: q
params.description: search run id, artifact, reviewer or configuration revision

verbs.returns: object: {reported, runs[], total, offset, limit, counts, in_flight[], last_failure, detail?} — `reported: false` when this worker emits no run events, and then the list is empty rather than inferred

verbs.name: dg.scan
verbs.summary: Run the deterministic scanner on one L0 artifact; a finding ≥ medium routes to L1b and no score clears it (INV-SEC-5). An explicit outcome is the manual override.

verbs.name: dg.scan_pending
verbs.summary: Scan every L0 artifact whose delay elapsed. Counts, never content.

verbs.name: dg.semantic_review
verbs.summary: ADR-0048/ADR-0053: ask the server-owned reviewer to look at one row. Every disposition it writes is reviewer_class='model' — a model is never laundered into a human signature by being triggered from a console. The caller supplies the subject and nothing else; the reviewer identity, the rendering, the scan event and the registry revision are read from the row.

params.name: settle
params.description: default true — settle the row if the disposition clears it

errors.-32602: unknown artifact: the id names no row in this quarantine
errors.-32014: the reviewer refused (no reviewable finding, unavailable backend, unusable reply); the row is unchanged

verbs.name: dg.settings
verbs.summary: The review worker's configuration: configured (on disk) beside effective (in this process), plus the drift between them and the field/choice tables a configuration surface renders.
verbs.description_note: Both halves, always. A settings view that shows only the file cannot tell the operator their last edit never took; one that shows only the runtime cannot tell them what a restart would bring back. Credential VALUES are never returned — `secrets` reports presence only.
verbs.returns: object: {configured, explicit, secrets, effective, etag, config_rev, drift[], fields, choices, runs}

verbs.name: dg.settings_save
verbs.summary: Compare-and-swap the configuration file, then apply it to this running daemon. Always both: a save that needs a restart to mean anything is a save the operator has to be told about twice.
verbs.description_note: The etag the caller was shown is REQUIRED; without it two editors overwrite each other silently. A stale etag returns `conflict` with the current etag and the current values so the caller can show what is actually there.

params.name: etag
params.description: the revision this draft was editing

verbs.returns: object: {ok, saved, applied, etag, config_rev, configured, secrets, effective, drift[], note} or {ok: false, conflict|errors}

verbs.name: dg.settings_validate
verbs.summary: Run a configuration draft through the real loader. Writes nothing, applies nothing — the call a form may make on every keystroke.

params.name: values
params.description: dotted `table.key` → value; only the keys being changed

verbs.returns: object: {ok, errors?} — field-keyed errors, never an exception

verbs.name: dg.settle_pending
verbs.summary: ADR-0048: under review.mode auto, promote every L2 row that meets k with no human required on its class — the deployment signs the promote, the integrator's boundary check applies unchanged. A no-op otherwise.

verbs.name: dg.sign
verbs.summary: Record a verdict as the calling principal (ADR-0082): a signed-in person's verdict is a human's, a key's or a socket peer's is a reviewer's and never satisfies a human requirement. With `promote: true` the signature and the promotion it was for happen in one call; a promotion the boundary refuses is reported in `promote.refused` and the signature stands.

verbs.name: dg.status
verbs.summary: Queue depths, journal tip, gate budget, role-specific gauges — or one artifact's lifecycle row.

params.name: artifact_id
params.description: one artifact instead of the deployment

verbs.name: dg.submit
verbs.summary: Queue an admitted artifact for the org gate (the outbox). Idempotent by artifact id.

verbs.name: dg.submit_drain
verbs.summary: Drain the outbox to the org gate now and pull outcomes (countersign / refuse) as peer events.
verbs.returns: object: {accepted, retry, stopped, refused, pulled, resolved, halted_reason?}

verbs.name: dg.tip
verbs.summary: The served head of an artifact's relation chain (ADR-0037).

verbs.name: dg.verify
verbs.summary: Walk the journal chain and verify every signature.

verbs.name: dg.why
verbs.summary: Every signed event about one artifact, in order — the provenance answer.

documents.openapi: docs/api/openapi.json and GET /openapi.json on this gate's loopback listener (any principal)
documents.docs_page: GET /app#/api — the app's API view, the interactive rendering of the OpenAPI document (GET /docs redirects there)
documents.org_openapi: doublegate-org: docs/api/openapi.json and GET /openapi.json on the keyed surface
documents.published: https://doublegate-io.github.io/api/ (snapshot of all four, stamped with the commit) — https://doublegate-io.github.io/llms.txt first
